clue.text: You can use this to order a large black tie

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in a black-tie dinner

blocks.clueFragment: You can use this to order
blocks.note: an order form is filled in to request goods
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone is told how to order an extra-large black tie for a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening reads as a recommendation of a shop or catalogue, but the whole phrase is a roundabout clue for a document you fill in.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-tie event is one with a strict dress code, i.e. a formal occasion.

clue.text: She's a bit vulgar but she's brill at work!

definitions.text: She's a bit vulgar but she's brill at work!

blocks.clueFragment: She's a bit vulgar but she's brill at work!
blocks.note: surface reading: a coarse woman who is nevertheless brilliant at her job
setter's reading: brill is a flatfish, so she handles fish at work, and market women of that trade were famous for coarse language

explanation.surface: A rough-mouthed woman who is nonetheless excellent at her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brill' looks like slang for brilliant; it is the name of a flatfish, the stock of a woman selling fish at market.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a woman who sells fish and, by extension, any coarse, loud-mouthed woman.

clue.text: Ladder and its short part

indicators.note: something short is cut off before its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a rung is a part of a ladder, the 'its' pointing back to the ladder

explanation.surface: A ladder and one of its pieces, sawn short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladder' is not the climbing kind in the definition: it is the British word for a line of unravelled stitches in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a ladder in stockings is the same thing Americans call a run.

clue.text: Quality attire but displayed badly

indicators.note: something displayed badly is put out in the wrong arrangement, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Clothes of fine quality, but shown off poorly in a shop window.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a characteristic or property, which is what a quality is.

clue.text: At back of reception English doctor enters extra date

definitions.note: a month rather than a single day

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, so only the end of reception is kept
to enter is to go inside, so these pieces sit within the word for extra

blocks.note: the final letter
over means extra, as in left over
E is the abbreviation for English
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An English doctor turns up at the back of a reception on an extra date.
explanation.definitionFit: A month is a broad calendar date, as in a deadline set for some time next month.

clue.text: Inspect some balls at Exeter?

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
Exeter is a cathedral city and the seat of a bishop, a see

explanation.surface: Someone is checking cricket balls at the ground in Exeter.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is cricket's unit of six deliveries; a see is the area ruled by a bishop, here the diocese based at Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or watch over work, which is what an inspector does.

clue.text: It's usually two or three shots to shoot this bird

definitions.text: It's usually two or three shots to shoot this

blocks.clueFragment: It's usually two or three shots to shoot this
blocks.note: first meaning: a golf score two under par, so a hole taken in two or three strokes on a par four or five
second meaning: the large bird of prey

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hunter needing several shots to bring a bird down; the shots are golf strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the term for two under par follows birdie for one under; it is also the name of a large raptor.

clue.text: Dog, we hear, you left in terrible mess at back of car

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of a word, so a letter that sounds like the word is taken
the back of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
a mess is a jumble, so all the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
the final letter

explanation.surface: A dog has left a dreadful mess on the back seat of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull terrier is a muscular dog breed with an egg-shaped head.

clue.text: Topless Victorian is mildly pornographic

indicators.note: without a top, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: the Victorians are proverbial for being prim and strait-laced

explanation.surface: A topless picture from the nineteenth century is a bit naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' fits the risqué surface so well it reads as description, but it tells you to behead the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slightly rude, a little smutty, is fairly called mildly pornographic.

clue.text: 80 per cent of Pacific island use odd language

indicators.note: four fifths of a five-letter word means dropping its last letter
odd letters are those in first, third and later odd positions

blocks.note: Tonga is a kingdom of South Pacific islands
the first and third letters

explanation.surface: Most of a Pacific island's people use a strange language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue is an older word for a language, as in mother tongue.

clue.text: Stokes gets run out — something to be wary of at the Gabba?

definitions.text: something to be wary of at the Gabba

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: England cricketer Ben Stokes is run out during an Ashes Test in Brisbane.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gabba is the cricket ground in Brisbane, where the summer sun is fierce; 'run out' is a cricket dismissal, but here 'out' alone mixes the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Heatstroke from too much sun is a real hazard for players and spectators at a hot Queensland ground.

clue.text: Frozen European in German hat

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the others

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
E is the abbreviation for European
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A European chilled to the bone wearing a German hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid is a literary adjective meaning icy cold, as frozen things are.

clue.text: Bad language results if son's this tiresome

indicators.note: the phrase says the longer word is the answer with a son attached, so the answer is that word with him taken away

blocks.note: swearing is foul or bad language
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A tiresome son provokes a parent into cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put S in front of the answer and you get a word for cursing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing describes something exhausting, a tiresome person or task that wears you down.

clue.text: Raise aid and act to distribute water

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the rest of the letters

explanation.surface: A call to raise money and act to supply clean water.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and the Balkans is a body of water.

clue.text: Cases in sessions heard at first with unexpected haste

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of each word is used
something unexpected is not in the expected order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letters of the two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Court cases heard hurriedly in sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' reads as legal cases heard in court; it means coverings for blades.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaths are close-fitting covers, cases for swords or knives.

clue.text: Those working in futures market giving a lot of money to bank staff

blocks.note: a fortune is a large sum of money
tellers serve customers at bank counters

explanation.surface: City traders making big sums for the bankers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Futures market' sounds like finance; the definition is cryptic, describing people who deal in predictions of the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Clairvoyants who predict what lies ahead are, playfully, working in a market for futures.

clue.text: Device helping to read endless correspondence about article from paper

indicators.note: with no end, so the final letter is cut off
about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around another
taking something from a word means it is removed

blocks.note: a letter is a piece of correspondence
a newspaper can be called an organ, as in a party's official organ
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something to help read through an unending stream of letters about a newspaper story.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held on a handle, an aid to reading.

clue.text: Move at speed with hint of madness?

definitions.text: Move at speed with hint of madness?

indicators.note: a hint is only a trace, so just the first letter of the word is used
to move the letters is to shift them into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A question: is this what it is to rush along with a touch of frenzy?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: 'Move' doubles as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden headlong rush of animals or people driven by panic, which is moving fast with a touch of madness.

clue.text: Is one's work on the way to being noticed?

definitions.text: Is one's work on the way to being noticed?

blocks.clueFragment: Is one's work on the way to being noticed?
blocks.note: surface reading: is someone's career on the road to recognition?
setter's reading: the work is literally drawn on the path, where passers-by may notice it

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way' reads as 'heading towards'; it really means physically on the walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A street performer who chalks pictures on the footway hopes passers-by will notice and toss coins.

clue.text: Showed up old partner and daughter embracing model

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
D is the abbreviation for daughter
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.definitionFit: To expose someone is to reveal their wrongdoing, to show them up.

clue.text: Start to tape old PM's endless gossip

clue.text: Damage caused by couple on motorway when upset

clue.text: Head to front of platform — one with a sea view

definitions.text: platform — one with a sea view

blocks.note: main means chief or head, as in the main office

explanation.surface: A traveller heads to the front of a railway platform for a view of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic name for the sea, which is why this platform has a sea view.
explanation.definitionFit: The maintop is the platform at the head of a sailing ship's mainmast, a lookout post over the ocean.

clue.text: Brown vest finally has funny fit

the final letter
